summary.headline: Sonata Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 15.4% YoY to Rs 2,445.2 Cr, but PAT fell YoY to Rs 116.4 Cr; International services USD revenue up only 0.9% YoY.
summary.overview: Management said the quarter marked the start of a return to growth, with International services up 1.0% QoQ in USD and domestic gross contribution up 19.3% YoY. International EBITDA margin was 15.5%, roughly flat QoQ, helped by higher utilisation (90.5%) and efficiency gains but offset by severance, proof-of-concept spend and wage increases. Consolidated PAT was Rs 116.4 Cr, up 7.7% QoQ but down YoY. Management guided to positive revenue and margin momentum in coming quarters, while flagging a Q3 ramp-down at one TMT top-10 account and some BFSI headwinds.

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Rs 797.9 Cr revenue (+9.3% YoY), USD 82.8 mn (+1.0% QoQ), 4 new customers added, top-10 clients 51% of revenue, 11 clients above USD 5 mn run-rate and 12 in the 3-5 mn band. Book-to-bill 1.18x; order book Rs 98.5 mn; AI-led order book Rs 24.2 mn (~25% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,655.6 Cr, gross contribution Rs 82 Cr (+19.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 47.3 Cr (+12.2% YoY). Management said OEM go-to-market headwinds are now behind it and it is focusing on gross contribution over revenue.

guidance_outlook: Management expects positive growth momentum in coming quarters despite Q3 headwinds in isolated BFSI and TMT accounts; the top-10 contribution is expected to rise.
EBITDA margin expected to improve from the Q2 base; no quantum given. Long-term aspiration of 18-20% margin reiterated versus 15.5% in Q2.
Severance (~50 bps) and one-time proof-of-concept investment (~100 bps) hit Q2 margin; management said further PoC spend may continue in Q3 but quantum is unknown.
AWS five-year strategic collaboration: team build-out over 2-3 quarters, execution expected from Q1 FY28; aim to double AWS-technology earnings gradually.
Domestic business: medium-term growth trajectory expected, no percentage growth guidance (declined to confirm 20-25%).
DSO to be maintained around 60 days for International services.
capex_capacity: Utilisation improved to 90.5% in Q2 from 88.5% in Q1, mainly from completion of ramp-up on one large deal.
Headcount (including domestic) 6,214 with attrition at 10%; onsite-offshore revenue mix 30:70.
Operationalised an inside sales group to support new domestic GTMs (enterprise IT services, GCC services, multi-cloud management).
Quant (acquired earlier) not impaired after March 2026 test; management said merger of Quant into Sonata may be considered in coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Top account dropped in Q1 on renewal and ramp-down of one program; management said this is behind the company, though a second TMT account will ramp down slightly in Q3 (order book in that account has grown).
Revenue growth of ~1% QoQ described as the start of a move from stability to growth; drivers cited as AI-native service delivery, legacy modernisation and AI-ready data.
Six horizontal offerings; three of them account for ~61% of injected pipeline (legacy modernisation, AI-powered engineering, AI-ready data).
Management is shifting from dependence on large deals (over USD 5 mn) to mid-size deals of USD 2-4 mn; cited a USD 4.2 mn deal this quarter.

Verticals: HLS growing consistently; BFSI improved after Quant-related account run-down; R&D under pressure; TMT ex top account good; retail to take 1-2 quarters to recover; logistics showing recovery.
Wins cited: cloud modernisation for a US food service equipment provider; mid-size accounts scaling faster under prove-and-scale model, though decision cycles are longer due to security regulation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the context behind the drop in a top customer, and the data revenue weakness (down ~50% YoY)?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-account drop came from renewals and a ramp-down of one program, which management says is behind it. Data weakness was attributed to the largest BFSI customer and the top account, both data-heavy; management expects data pipeline and order book to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the EBITDA walk: wage hike, severance and PoC investment.
qa_highlights.answer: Severance cost was ~50 bps and one-time PoC investment ~100 bps. Wage increase for lower management (about 60% of staff) hit EBITDA as expected but was not quantified. Management said Q3 PoC spend is undetermined.

qa_highlights.question: Will the domestic business return to mid-teen gross contribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a percentage and said only that medium-term growth trajectory is expected, citing current GTMs and OEM engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-account renewal stress emerge after earlier comments that renewals were on track, and what verticals drive growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-account ramp-down was in one program; positive traction expected from next quarter. HLS growing; BFSI recovering; R&D under pressure; TMT ex top account healthy; mid-size accounts scaling faster.

qa_highlights.question: What is Microsoft exposure (Sell-To and Sell-With) in IT services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said details can be provided but gave no figures on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What margin levers exist and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Aspiration remains 18-20%; management expects margin improvement from Q2 base, with quantum to be disclosed with results. Said revenue growth of ~1% is the first growth step after four to five quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AWS deal's ramp-up timing and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Five-year SCA; team build over 2-3 quarters; execution from Q1 FY28. Aim is to double AWS-technology earnings gradually; no ballpark contribution given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there impairment risk on Quant?
qa_highlights.answer: No impairment recorded; last test in March 2026 with auditor confirmation. Impairment to be reassessed periodically; merger into Sonata possible.

risks_watch: Top-10 concentration: one TMT account to ramp down in Q3 and a BFSI account faces isolated Q3 headwinds.
Consolidated PAT declined YoY and International USD growth is near zero (+0.9% YoY).
Margin recovery depends on unquantified Q3 PoC investment and whether severance costs recur.
Domestic revenue fell 33.9% QoQ; the business is reported on gross contribution, so comparability needs checking.
Quant goodwill: impairment test next due after governance review; merger possible.
Microsoft Sell-To/Sell-With exposure figures promised but not provided on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on direction and the return to growth, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to quantify Q3 margin, PoC spend, the domestic growth rate, and Microsoft exposure. Tone was defensive on the top-account drop and the data revenue decline, which it attributed to isolated, now-resolved issues.
key_quotes: In this quarter we are moving the needle from stability to towards growth, which is represented in this 1%.

So, this one time proof of delivery, depending on what customer wants and what is the situation of the deal, which is not a planned kind of an investment, it can be structured for the next four quarters kind of thing.
Our aspiration is to maintain the margin between 18% to 20%.

adds.what: AWS five-year strategic collaboration team build-out (people, not plants)

growth.why: Management guides to positive growth and margin momentum from a ~1% QoQ USD revenue uptick, with book-to-bill 1.18x and 18-20% margin aspiration unquantified; Q3 headwinds in BFSI/TMT flagged, and no capacity additions or revenue percentage guidance were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: International EBITDA margin 15.5% in Q2 with severance (~50 bps) and PoC (~100 bps) one-offs absorbed; management expects improvement from the Q2 base, aspiration 18-20%, but no quantum given and Q3 PoC spend undetermined.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation rose to 90.5% from 88.5%, but no new plant, line or branch was discussed; the only build-out is AWS team hiring over 2-3 quarters, which is people, not capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: International USD revenue grew only +1.0% QoQ and +0.9% YoY, with book-to-bill 1.18x and the top-10 contribution expected to rise, but a TMT ramp-down in Q3 and BFSI headwinds weigh on near-term volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 90.5% is above the 80% threshold with no new capacity announced, but the call gave no capex plan or amount, and the Quant merger is a corporate action rather than capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only to 'positive momentum' from ~1% QoQ USD growth, gave no percentage revenue guidance and declined to quantify domestic growth, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: A top-10 TMT account ramps down in Q3, a BFSI account faces isolated headwinds, and PoC spend may continue with unknown quantum, against USD growth of only 0.9% YoY.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six horizontal offerings with AI-native delivery, legacy modernisation and AI-ready data cited, and AWS collaboration execution from Q1 FY28, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Quant merger into Sonata
rows.why: Management said a merger of Quant into Sonata may be considered in coming quarters; Quant was not impaired after the March 2026 test, and no decision or amount was given.

rows.label: AWS five-year strategic collaboration ramp
rows.why: Team build-out over 2-3 quarters with execution from Q1 FY28, aiming to gradually double AWS-technology earnings, but no ballpark contribution was given.

rows.label: International DSO normalisation to ~60 days
rows.why: DSO fell to 52 days from 60 days, partly from advance collections, and management guided it back to about 60 days, which means a working-capital release may reverse.

tone.note: Management was confident about the turn to growth, mid-size deal shift and AWS collaboration, but declined to quantify Q3 margin, PoC spend, domestic growth and Microsoft exposure; analysts pressed on the top-account drop, data revenue decline and the sustainability of the ~1% QoQ uptick.
